subject: Horizon Labs: proposed latency corridor & escalation plan
messages:
From: Alice Zhang <alice@horizonlabs.ai>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.ai
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@horizonlabs.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Request: tighter latency corridor for production pilot

Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the performance looked promising. As we move into a 6-week pilot with internal users, Horizon Labs is evaluating an SLA addendum so we can commit internal seats and run a front-line trial. Specifically our product team is asking whether Redwood can agree to a P95 latency corridor of <= 150ms for our "low-latency inference" route during business hours (PST).

We understand this is a bespoke ask and are happy to discuss compensation/term trade-offs. Can you connect us to the right folks at Redwood (ops, product, legal) to scope feasibility, monitoring, and escalation? We also have procurement deadlines the week of March 22.

Thanks — would appreciate a quick read on feasibility.

— Alice
Alice Zhang
Head of Product, Horizon Labs
alice@horizonlabs.ai

Attachment: horizon-pilot-context.pdf (summary, 2 pages)

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: tighter latency corridor for production pilot

Team — forwarding Horizon's request. Quick asks:

1) Feasibility: can we support a committed P95 <= 150ms for their dedicated route during 9am–6pm PT for the pilot (anticipated 40 qps bursty)? If not, what mitigations (burst capacity, auto-fallback to higher-latency tier) look viable?
2) Observability: what monitoring and alerting would we need to include so they can trust the commitment (traces, token-level latency breakdown, synthetic probes)?
3) Legal/Commercial: what contract language & term/credits model should we propose for a time-limited pilot?

They are strategic — small ARR now but fast expansion potential. Procurement deadline week of Mar 22, so we should aim for an internal approach by Tues 16th. Can folks reply with short bullets and any blockers. I'll coordinate a 30m sync if helpful.

Thanks — Chloe
Chloe Martin
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0108

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 08:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: tighter latency corridor for production pilot

Chloe / Grace — quick engineering read:

- Baseline: for their expected profile (40 qps, median seq len ~120 tokens), a dedicated pool with 2 x A100-equivalent allocation plus prefix caching should get us comfortably under 150ms P95 in steady-state.
- Burst risk: if they spike beyond provisioned qps or run longer sequences, P95 will increase. To protect SLOs we can offer: 1) scheduled burst buffers (extra capacity at known windows), 2) circuit-breaker fallback to a slightly lower-cost, higher-latency model variant with automatic retries and clear telemetry.
- Telemetry: we can emit per-route P95/P50 rolling windows, synthetic probes every 5m, and a token-level latency breakdown. We should include an SLA metric tag so their monitoring pulls directly from our metrics.
- Ops burden: this will require a temporary runbook for on-call rotations during the pilot and an internal playbook for fallback triggers. I estimate 1 SRE FTE equivalent across the pilot unless we automate the fallback.

Open questions for product/leadership: do we want to commit to hard P95 numbers or offer a conditional corridor with defined fallback & credits? The latter reduces risk for Redwood.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal SW Eng, Serving Runtime

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: tighter latency corridor for production pilot

Chloe / team — legal view in bullets:

- We can agree to a time-limited P95 commitment for a pilot provided we include narrow carveouts (force majeure, scheduled maintenance, third-party infra failures) and an explicit fallback policy.
- Contract should define measurement windows (5-min rolling vs daily aggregates), enforcement (credits capped at X% of pilot fees), and an acceptance testing period before the SLA goes live.
- Avoid open-ended uptime credits; propose a credit table tied to verified breaches with a cap equal to one month of pilot fees.
- Require Horizon to provide production traffic profile and to notify about any load-generating test windows.

I can draft a one-page SLA addendum and a short annex for monitoring & runbook. If leadership wants a firmer number we need executive sign-off on the credit cap.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhang <alice@horizonlabs.ai>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@horizonlabs.ai>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: tighter latency corridor for production pilot — proposed path forward

Hi Alice / Raj — thanks for outlining the ask. Internal alignment below and a proposed mutual action plan to hit your procurement window.

Summary of Redwood position (short):
- Feasibility: We can offer a pilot-specific P95 corridor of <= 150ms during 9am–6pm PT with the following guardrails: dedicated capacity, prefix caching, and a pre-defined fallback to a higher-latency model variant if sustained traffic exceeds X qps.
- Observability: we will provide per-route P95/P50 dashboards, synthetic probes every 5 minutes, and a shared alert channel.
- Commercials & risk: pilot SLA will be time-limited (6 weeks), with a credit regime capped at one month of pilot fees for verified breaches. Carveouts for maintenance and third-party outages will be included.

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
1) This week (by Tue 16 Mar): Horizon to share expected traffic profile (qps, sequence length distribution) and any planned test windows. Redwood will send a one-page SLA addendum + runbook.
2) Wed 17 Mar: 30m alignment call to walk the runbook and escalation steps (we'll invite SRE/CS).
3) Fri 19 Mar: sign SLA addendum and enable dedicated pilot pool.
4) Week of Mar 22: pilot kickoff (monitoring live).

Attachments: horizon_commitment_matrix_v1.xlsx (proposed corridors & fallback tiers), latency-runbook-draft.pdf (ops playbook)

If that timeline works for you, please reply and share the traffic artifact. We'll loop in Vivek for an executive sign-off email once we have the traffic numbers.

Thanks — Chloe
Chloe Martin
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.ai
